asks: what the census's window costs per leg, from measurements that actually paid

window.why: row counts, never a date range evaluated at run time (SPEC 3.18 (4))

rate.why: the settled serverless rate: five endpoints billed on 2026-08-08 read within 1% of it. Every projection in this repo since sku-b has used this one field

drift.why: a contract term, not a measurement, applied to the whole billed second count

job_shape.source: scripts/positions_gm4_skub.py :: JOB_TIMEOUT_S / JOB_TTL_S / IDLE_TAIL_SECONDS; results/serving_srv2d_smoke.json :: deployment.endpoint.workersMax
job_shape.why: a cap is a bound in DOLLARS and a session is also a bound in wall clock. One worker at a 900 s execution timeout means the seconds below are serial and the job count is what a session has to be packed into — SPEC 3.17 (10)(c) is the rule that no single job may be capable of billing past the remaining cap

comment.task: T1 with the parent post — market_pulse.loop.COMMENT_TASK

ledger.why: cumulative against that session's own anchor, so the parity step is the difference — and it is an ACCOUNT delta, not a per-leg price. The per-leg figures below come from srv2d_cost.json, which applies the settled rate to measured seconds and agrees with the account to about 1%

rows_scored.why: the comment half of the 758: 400 comments_test rows, 0 parse and 0 api failures

composition.why: the unit cost is BLENDED across those three and this window is pure T1. Direction of the error, from the smoke's own per-row seconds, results/serving_srv2d_smoke.json :: rows[*].worker_seconds — T1 5.176/4.319/4.368/4.408 against T2 3.978/3.903/3.991/3.958, n=4 each — the comment task is the SLOWER of the two, so a blended rate under-prices a pure-comment window rather than over-pricing it

paid_measurement.floor: the RunPod balance delta lags the resource by minutes and the itemised ledger by hours (this endpoint's row had settled 1 538 s of 3 793 s when the session closed). Every figure here is a FLOOR, so the ratio against the pod is a lower bound.

unit_cost.why: srv-2d's whole parity pass over 758 rows on the serverless endpoint, its own boot amortised INSIDE it. The conservative corner: nothing else has to be added to it
unit_cost.note: the boot is already inside the unit cost; only the idle tail is added
unit_cost.seconds_are: IMPLIED — the dollars divided by the settled rate, not a measured wall clock. The marginal corner below is the one whose seconds were counted

marginal_plus_boot.why: the same session's per-row seconds with the cold start taken out — the corner a boot is added to. It is the one that answers «how many more rows fit under this cap»

boot.why: one cold start on that endpoint, paid once per session before any row is scored

marginal_plus_boot.seconds_are: MEASURED per-row seconds plus that endpoint's measured cold start

leaflet_page.task: positions_post_gm4, one page per call — SPEC 3.17 (4)

ledger.why: the whole session against its own anchor: 138 sources, cap $0.65

population.why: the contract's briefing says the session «bought 138 pages»; the record says 138 SOURCES — 108 pages and 30 text rows. The page marginal below is measured over the 108, which is what per_gate[-1].calls_done counts

report_line.quote: page leg   108 pages sent (of 159 available, 19 posts) in 7 job(s), largest 7.99 MB
report_line.why: the same arithmetic in that session's report: 462.173 s over 108 calls. (711.102 - 248.929) / 108 = 4.2794, which is the field cited above

marginal_plus_boot.why: the LAST in-run gate of the skub2 session, taken when 108 of the 138 sources were done and every one of them was a page — so this is the page leg's own marginal, and it is the number the cap stop itself acted on

boot.why: that session's cold start, paid once

warmup.why: the two non-gold calls SPEC 3.17 (9) requires before either leg touches gold

whole_window.usd_source: the CONSERVATIVE corner of each leg, summed
whole_window.seconds_source: the MARGINAL corner of each leg — the only one whose seconds were counted rather than divided out of a price. Dollars and wall clock come from different corners on purpose, and each field says which
whole_window.why: This is the number the window ruling turns on and it is the reason this contract ends at a STOP: the whole window does not fit in what the phase has left

buys.why: conservative uses the unit cost (srv-2d's boot inside it), optimistic the marginal plus one boot. The two rates differ by 9% and neither is settled — the account reading behind both is a FLOOR (Dv33)

at_the_conservative_rate.why: what the cap was solved against — this is the number that must stay under it

at_the_marginal_rate.why: the same rows on measured seconds: the wall clock and the job count

budget.cap_source: scripts/runpod_guard.py :: PHASE_CAP_USD (the line that ENFORCES it)
budget.note: 5c2-prep-a: cap 25 → 30 per SPEC 3.18 (3); phase ledger repaired

no_paid_measurement.why: both legs have one, so no row is marked NO PAID MEASUREMENT. The candidate that did NOT become a source is named beside it

candidate_read_and_not_used.holds: row counts and failure counts — 400 + 250 + 108 rows, 0 parse failures, 0 api failures — and `parity.cap_usd` 4.0. It carries no seconds and no dollars
candidate_read_and_not_used.why: a candidate is not a source until its number is on the screen. Its rows are used above (they are what the unit cost is per) and its cost is not, because it has none: srv2d_cost.json is where that session's price was written
